newsitem.title: INDIA: Suzuki, India match wits over car maker's future.
newsitem.headline: Suzuki, India match wits over car maker's future.

text.p: Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp (SMC) called on Sunday for a mutually acceptable managing director in its Indian car venture after the government, an equal partner, insisted on naming the next choice for the post.
A tug-of-war between the two has raised questions on the future of Maruti Udyog Ltd, which controls more than 70 percent of India's car market.
India will insist on naming Maruti's next managing director, Industry Minister Murasoli Maran was quoted as saying on Sunday.
"Why should we forego our right? We have waited for five years and it is our right now as per the joint venture agreement," he told the Press Trust of India (PTI).
Maran discussed Maruti's future on Saturday with Suzuki's visiting chief executive officer Osamu Suzuki.
Maruti's managing director, R.C. Bhargava, is due to retire at the end of August.
"For the successful working of a 50-50 joint venture, a mutually accceptable managing director is essential," Suzuki said in a statement.

Suzuki came to discuss the issue under an understanding that the next managing director would be appointed in full consultation with the Japanese partner, it said, adding that in 1992 Bhargava was named after such a prrocess.

Suzuki said it favoured an early appointment of the managing director to ensure a smooth succession. "This is normal business practice and it is considered useful to have some overlap period," the statement said.
"This subject was discussed but no conclusion could be reached regarding any person," it added.

"It was, however, agreed that the managing director should preferably be an internal candidate. The government of India's view was that there was still plenty of time available for the decision," the statement said.

Suzuki entered India in 1984, much before the start of an economic liberalisation programme in 1991, which brought in keen rivals. The venture helped Suzuki, but it is now fighting a tough battle to retain its hold over Maruti.

Asked whether he would accept Bhargava as the joint venture's chairman, a post currently held by a government bureaucrat, Maran replied: "We will cross the bridge when it comes. Anyway we did not talk about any names and it would be discussed only next month."

Suzuki is keen to push an ambitious 15 billion rupee ($419 million) expansion plan in Maruti to meet competition from car markers like South Korea's Daewoo Corp and the U.S.'s Ford Motor Co and General Motors Corp.
Daewoo holds a majority in its Indian venture, Daewoo Motor India Ltd, which plans to launch in 1998 a small car expected to compete with Maruti's hottest-selling 800cc model.
"During the discussions the earlier decision to finance the implementation of the expansion project and the engine shop by internal resources and debt was reconfirmed by SMC," it said.

There was no talk of a change in the equity structure or disinvestment by either party, it said, adding the meeting took place on the understanding of the government's position that the equity structure would not change and follow earlier agreements.
Maruti is estimated to have produced 338,690 cars in 1996/97 (April-March), compared with 275,411 in 1995/96.
Maruti posted a net profit of 5.01 billion rupees ($140 million) in 1996/97, up from 4.28 billion in 1995/96.
But Bhargava said it would be difficult to maintain the profit in 1997/98 as a substantial rise in output was difficult.
